minutes.headline: Town-proposed bylaw rewrite would blend the COA director's duties into the board's; feedback due by Dec. 2
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging spent much of the meeting reacting to a late-arriving, town-drafted revision of its bylaws that appears to fold the director's duties into the board's own charge, and agreed to review it and respond by an early-December deadline. The board also heard a tri-board FY27 budget presentation with a stated funding request, discussed a proposed assistant-director/program-coordinator restructuring and grant-seeking priorities, ratified a prior vote on 41A tax-deferral work, and reviewed a busy fall calendar of senior programs and fundraisers.

what_happened.line: A town-drafted rewrite of Article 3 would fold the COA director's duties into the board's own charge; the board held it for review and asked for the director's job description to compare against it.
The board ratified its earlier vote authorizing work with the town on a 41A tax-deferral article for town meeting, unanimously.
The director presented the COA's FY27 budget request as part of a joint tri-board review with the finance committee, school committee and select board.
The board told the director to bring any assistant-director/program-coordinator restructuring ideas to the full board before taking them to the tri-board in the future.
A vote to let the director keep pursuing grant-funding opportunities with the town was recorded, but the outcome was not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: A bylaw change to who runs the senior center's day-to-day duties is up for board feedback before a Dec. 2 deadline, and residents who use COA programs may want to weigh in.
The 41A article would widen who qualifies to defer property tax, a mechanism some senior households use to put off a tax bill until a home is sold.
The COA's FY27 budget request is part of the town's tri-board process that ultimately shapes the property tax rate voters see.
